title: PTGui tutorial part 4: Editing and viewing spherical panoramas — technique timeline and topics
summary: This PTGui Part 4 tutorial demonstrates viewing and editing spherical panoramas using the equirectangular projection, starting from an auto-aligned panorama and progressing through leveling, edge behavior, and viewing options. The video explains the Align Images workflow (control points, optimization, and projection choice), manual and bubble-level leveling concepts via the Panorama Editor, and the geometric implications of the equirectangular format (pole and edge wrapping). It also covers preview pathways (Preview, Detail Viewer, and interactive viewers), export options (Create Panorama as JPEG/TIFF and website publishing), and an overview of the Image Parameters and Optimizer tabs, with notes about future tutorials such as cube-face editing and vertical-line control points.

sections.title: Intro and equirectangular projection overview
sections.description: Introduction to the video and the equirectangular projection, described as the projection used to display and store a fully spherical 360 by 180 degree panorama.

sections.title: Align Images workflow and auto-setup
sections.description: Overview of the Align Images button, which generates control points, optimizes the project, deletes the worst control points, fits the panorama, selects a projection (equirectangular for this case), and attempts to level the panorama.

sections.title: Panorama leveling and tripod setup
sections.description: Discussion of leveling results when the tripod was leveled with a bubble level, and the option to use the Panorama Editor to level the panorama if the tripod wasn't leveled.

sections.title: Manual leveling and control point types
sections.description: Explanation of manual leveling by dragging to adjust pitch and yaw, and rolling with right-mouse dragging; mention that vertical line type control points offer precise leveling in a separate tutorial.

sections.title: Equirectangular projection properties and seam behavior
sections.description: Explanation of why the equirectangular view is used and how the North/South Poles become edges in the image; discussion of how the left/right edges wrap and become a continuous image, with implications for editing near the edges.

sections.title: Editing cautions for equirectangular images
sections.description: Advice on avoiding visible discontinuities when editing or applying local filters near the image edges, and noting that global adjustments (levels, brightness) apply consistently, while local filters can create seams.

sections.title: Preview and viewing options
sections.description: Introduction to multiple preview modalities: a quick Preview tab, a Detail Viewer for full-resolution inspection (zenith/nadir), and an interactive Panorama Viewer with consistent grid display.

sections.title: Export, web viewing, and quick previews
sections.description: Overview of exporting the panorama as a non-interactive JPEG/TIFF, using a separate viewer for interactivity, and using PTGui's Publish to Website for a quick interactive web page.

sections.title: Image Parameters and Optimizer overview
sections.description: Brief look at the Image Parameters tab (positioned per-image settings and exposure offset, including multi-select edits) and the Optimizer tab, with mention of the Advanced button and help texts accessed via SHIFT.
